title: A Fork Fest
reviewNotes: Captions and native complete diagrams reviewed. Native18–21 establish the complete nine-piece later root White Ka1/Nc4/b2/h4 against Kc5/Qe3/a6/c6/a4. Only Nxe3 is source play in the new independently supplied h-pawn/c-pawn race. Nxe3/Kd6/h5/c5/h6/c4/h7/c3/h8=Q/c2/Qa8/Kd7/Qxa6 reaches a complete seven-piece ending with White Ka1/Qa6/Ne3/b2 against Kd7/a4/c2, Black to move. Exact saved tablebase evidence says DRAW, and c1=Q+ is the sole drawing Black move; every other Black move permits a White win. The separate conditional-leaf draft verifies the root and c1=Q+ with the project CLI. This refutes an automatic conversion claim for this selected greedy capture, not the unproved nine-piece root outcome. The expanded sixteen-ply exploration still lacks a complete certificate after runs of 1,945 and 2,758 nodes; it preserves 423 exact supported query records and 852 partial legal White choices. The current verifier limit remains twelve; no limit or verified label changed. Future analysis must avoid the drawing c-pawn resource, check all Black defenses and supply a complete eligible root strategy. All prior drafts, source images/captions and review history remain preserved. Final bounded exploration removed the previously forced Qa8 transfer and widened independent engine candidate selection to five choices; this did not complete a root certificate. It visited 1,886 nodes, adding 60 exact supported responses for 483 total saved probes. The merged partial policy preserves previous choices and contains 882 legal White choices. All earlier root and conditional-leaf limitations still apply; current project verification remains capped at twelve plies. Recurring continuation is being disabled after repeated incomplete searches. Dedicated complete larger-position proof is required, not additional source material for this available source.
transcript: White's brilliant idea is C5 check, now forking the king and queen. And of course, if nothing is done, the queen is going to be taken. And if the king takes [music] this pawn, now unfortunately you have placed your king and queen in the perfect position to get forked by a knight. And now white is going to be able to win the queen and easily win the game. But of course, black is not that naive and is under no obligation to take this [music] pawn with the king. Instead, the queen is going to be taken like this. And now with a queen for three minor pieces, black is at the very least going to be able to hold the if not play for some tricks. But white has a brilliant resource in this position that starts with the beautiful knight [music] to A4 check, forking the king and queen anyway. Except at this time, the knight can just be captured like this. And now it might seem like black is simply out of the woods. There is no continuation for white. But that could not be further from the truth because there is another brilliant sacrifice incoming with bishop to E3. With only a knight and a bishop left, white gives up the bishop entirely. The queen is pinned to the king and so of course, it has to take this bishop or it's going to get captured on the next move. But now we have placed the queen and the king exactly where we want them to be for a knight fork on C4, attacking them both. The king has to move. We're going to win the queen and the game. If you love incredible chess, follow for more.
